name: University of Salford

settingEvidence.evidence: Our campus, Peel Park, offers the best of both worlds: state-of-the-art learning facilities set against beautiful green space

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK (Home) students starting in 2027 (2027/28). This is the stated tuition fee cap for 2027/28, and Salford's course pages list £10,050 a year for full-time Home students. Fees may rise each year in line with inflation, up to the government limit.

source.evidence: In England and Wales, the tuition fee cap for 2026/27 will be £9,790 and for 2027/28 will be £10,050.

livingCosts.text: Salford's cost guide for a single student renting privately in Greater Manchester gives minimum rent of £1,100 a month for a house share (£14,000 a year) or £1,300 a month for a studio (£15,500 a year), before bills, food and travel. Rooms in Salford's partner hall, Peel Park Quarter, are priced on the Campus Living Villages website, not on Salford's own pages.

source.evidence: £1,100 - House share (based on the local rental market prices)

openDays.text: Next undergraduate open days: Saturday 7 November 2026 and Saturday 12 December 2026 (in person, 09:30 to 16:00, across Salford's three campuses).

source.evidence: Our next Open Days take place on Saturday 7 November and Saturday 12 December. You can book your place now.

contextual.summary: Home-fee UCAS applicants in the most disadvantaged group of UCAS's Multiple Equality Measure, or who are care experienced or seeking sanctuary, can get an offer up to 16 UCAS points (about two grades) lower.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to 16 UCAS Tariff points, or the equivalent of two grades, below the typical entry requirements for your chosen course.

criteria.detail: Group 1 of UCAS's Multiple Equality Measure 1 (MEM1) or Multiple Equality Measure 2 (MEM2). The MEM groups combine local-area higher-education participation (POLAR4), area deprivation (Index of Multiple Deprivation and Income Deprivation Affecting Children Index), the type of school you attend, free school meal eligibility and whether you attended an independent or state school. Group 1 is the students least likely to enter higher education.
Care experienced: spent any amount of time in care at any point in their life.
Seeking sanctuary: seeking asylum or granted refugee status by the UK government (international students are otherwise not eligible).

contextual.rulesText: No separate application: Salford uses the contextual data in your UCAS application. You must live in the UK, apply through UCAS for a full-time undergraduate course, be assessed as paying home fees and be studying three A levels, a BTEC Extended Diploma or a mix of A levels and BTEC (T Levels are not currently included). Meeting the criteria does not guarantee an offer. If you qualify for both a contextual and a Local Talent offer, the contextual offer takes precedence.

source.evidence: If you fall into Group 1 of either MEM1 or MEM2, you will be eligible for a contextual offer.

courses.notes: Salford's main Economics degree: the course finder lists no separate single-honours Economics. Dual accreditation with the Chartered Management Institute (CMI). First year covers micro and macroeconomics; later years include development economics, econometrics and game theory alongside core business modules. The Salford Alternative Entry Scheme (SAES) can assess applicants who do not meet the stated entry criteria but can show they could succeed on the course.
